# 30-day plan to grow from 140 subscribers

## Check capacity first

If we double, we deliver 280 boxes every Saturday morning. Before spending anything on marketing, check three things:
- **Baking:** can the oven and the team bake 280 boxes for one Saturday?
- **Delivery:** with 3 people and cargo bikes, can we get 280 boxes out within the promised window?
- **Cash:** can we pay for twice the flour, packaging and hours before the new revenue comes in?

If any of these can't take more than about 200 boxes, fix it first or cap sign-ups with a waitlist. A waitlist also helps sales, because people want what they can't get yet. Growing faster than we can deliver will cost us the subscribers we already have.

## Doubling in 30 days is unlikely, so set the target at about +60 to +80

Going from 140 to 280 in 30 days with €300 is very aggressive. Doubling is still worth aiming for, but treat +60 to +80 as a strong month. The good news is that the timing helps: it's 19 November, and December is the best month of the year to sell food subscriptions as gifts.

## The plan, from biggest lever to smallest

**1. Turn current subscribers into recruiters (week 1). This is the biggest lever.**
- Put a free "give one to a neighbour" box voucher card in every box on Saturday 21 and 28 November.
- When the neighbour subscribes, the person who referred them gets a free week. The new subscriber gets their first box at half price.
- Cost: only ingredients and the free weeks, and we pay those only when someone converts. None of it comes out of the €300.
- If 30–40% of subscribers hand out a card and a third of those neighbours sign up, that's about 15–20 new subscribers per wave. Run two waves.

**2. Christmas gift subscriptions (launch this week, sell until about 20 December).**
- Offer a 4-week gift for €72 and a 12-week gift for about €200 (a small discount), with a nice printed card.
- Pitch it at subscribers ("give one to your parents or your neighbour"), at shop customers, and at local employers as a staff or client gift. One office ordering 10 boxes is worth more than a week of flyers.
- Gift subscribers stay with us for 4–12 weeks. Our job is to convert them into paying subscribers in January.

**3. Convert the people already coming into the shop (every day).**
- These are our warmest prospects. Put a sign at the till ("Get this delivered every Saturday, €18, cancel anytime") with a QR code, and have whoever is on the counter ask every regular.
- Offer a first box for €9 to anyone who signs up in the shop.
- Count how many we ask and how many sign up each day. This is often the single biggest source of new subscribers.

**4. Sampling on the streets we already deliver to (weekends 2–4).**
- Pick the 3–4 streets or buildings with the most subscribers, so new customers there add almost no delivery time.
- Leave a small sample, like a mini loaf or a cardamom bun, with a flyer and the half-price first-box offer. A Saturday stall outside the shop or at a local Christmas market works the same way.

**5. Win back people who cancelled.**
- Send a personal message from you: "We've missed you. Your first box back is on us before Christmas." It's cheap and usually converts better than reaching new people.

## How to spend the €300

| Item | € |
|---|---|
| Printed referral and gift cards, flyers | 90 |
| Sampling ingredients and packaging | 120 |
| Christmas market stall fee or local Instagram/Facebook ads around 3 km | 90 |

## Making it stick

- **Lower the barrier to subscribing:** say clearly that people can skip or pause any week and cancel anytime. Fear of commitment is the main objection to subscriptions.
- **Plan the holiday Saturdays:** in 2026, Christmas Day falls on a Friday, so we still have deliveries on Saturday 26 December and Saturday 2 January. Decide now whether we deliver those weeks, skip them, or let subscribers pause. Otherwise cancellations will pile up in January.
- **Track weekly:** new subscribers by source (referral, gift, shop, sampling, win-back), cancellations, and cost per new subscriber. After two weeks, put more effort into whichever source is working.

If you can tell me how many boxes we could bake and deliver on one Saturday, and roughly how many people come into the shop each week, I can turn this into a week-by-week schedule with targets for each source.
